bib.title: VL-BERT: Pre-training of Generic Visual-Linguistic Representations

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "VL-BERT: Pre-training of Generic Visual-Linguistic Representations", Weijie Su, Xizhou Zhu, Yue Cao, Bin Li, Lewei Lu, Furu Wei, Jifeng Dai (USTC and Microsoft Research Asia). ICLR 2020, arXiv 1908.08530v4 (18 Feb 2020).

COVERAGE: I read all 58,097 of 58,097 extracted characters: body, Table 5 (Appendix A.1), the training settings (A.2) and the attention visualisation (A.3). I skimmed the references for origins. Figure captions come from figures.py.

One fact matters for the target paragraph. VL-BERT came out before UNITER (1909.11740), so it never compares against UNITER. Its comparisons are ViLBERT, LXMERT, VisualBERT, B2T2 and Unicoder-VL, all marked "concurrent". That means "how it differs from UNITER" comes from my reading of the design, not from anything this paper says.

HOW IT DIFFERS (author's framing, p.3, ~char 11000-12500)
- From ViLBERT and LXMERT: it uses one stream, with "a uniﬁed architecture based on Transformers without any restriction on the attention patterns... they interact early and freely". The authors say: "We found that our uniﬁed model of VL-BERT outperforms such two-stream designs."
- It differs from all of the concurrent works in three pretraining choices:
  1. It drops Sentence-Image Relationship Prediction (image-text matching): "is of no help in pre-training visual-linguistic representations."
  2. It adds text-only corpora (BooksCorpus and English Wikipedia), which "improves the generalization over long and complex sentences."
  3. It fine-tunes the Fast R-CNN end to end, and it masks raw pixels instead of feature maps: "the masking operation is conducted on the input raw pixels, other than the feature maps".
- Contrast with UNITER (my inference from the note, not stated in the paper): UNITER, per the note, found image-text matching one of its two strongest objectives. VL-BERT, with a different setup, found that the same matching loss hurt.

LIMITS
- No seeds, error bars or repeated runs anywhere. Many of the ablation differences are 0.0 to 0.8 points.
- The ablation uses 0.5x fine-tuning epochs and BASE only. The main tables have no BASE test numbers for VCR or VQA.
- No detector cost is reported: no inference latency and no FLOPs for Faster R-CNN. Fine-tuning the detector end to end adds training cost, which is also not quantified. The only compute given is GPU count and iteration count.
- The masked-RoI labels are Faster R-CNN predictions, not human labels ("The category label predicted by pre-trained Faster R-CNN is set as the ground-truth").
- The matching-loss result has only a guessed explanation, and the authors do not test it.
- No retrieval or captioning results. The authors list captioning as future work.
- The comparisons are against arXiv preprints of the time. Dated: detector-region tokens, which ViT-based models later replaced.

BUILDS ON
- BERT (Devlin et al., 2018), initialised from BERT-BASE and BERT-LARGE
- Transformer (Vaswani et al., 2017)
- Fast R-CNN (Girshick, 2015) and Faster R-CNN (Ren et al., 2015)
- BUTD (Anderson et al., 2018) and Visual Genome (Krishna et al., 2017), for the region features
- Relation Networks (Hu et al., 2018), for the sine/cosine box geometry embedding
- WordPiece (Wu et al., 2016)
- Conceptual Captions (Sharma et al., 2018) and BooksCorpus (Zhu et al., 2015)
- BERT-as-MRF (Wang & Cho, 2019)
- Video precursors: VideoBERT (Sun et al., 2019b) and CBT (Sun et al., 2019a)
- R2C (Zellers et al., 2019), for the VCR protocol
- MAttNet (Yu et al., 2018), for the detected boxes

CODE: none in the paper. It points to https://github.com/jackroos/VL-BERT.

FIGURES
- Figure 1, p.5: the architecture. The token, segment, position and visual-feature embeddings are summed; RoI pixels are zeroed before Fast R-CNN; both masked objectives are shown. It shows the single stream and the pixel-level masking faster than prose.
- Figure 2, p.8: input and output formats for VCR, VQA and RefCOCO+ ([CLS] answer classification, [MASK] answer prediction, per-RoI classification). Useful for showing how one encoder serves three task heads.
- Figure 3, p.15: attention maps from text tokens to RoIs (BertViz), qualitative only.

PROBLEMS
- The checkmark columns in Table 4 are garbled in extraction, so which components each row contains is my reconstruction from the prose in Section 4.3. Check against the PDF page 10 table before citing row contents.
